guide.title: Esquilino, Rome: Termini, piazza Vittorio and Santa Croce in Gerusalemme
guide.intro: Esquilino is the fifteenth of Rome's twenty-two rioni by toponymic code, R. XV, and it lies in Municipio Roma I. Termini station stands in it, and so does piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, the porticoed square laid out under the 1873 master plan and built from 1880, with a Severan fountain and a seventeenth-century alchemical doorway standing in its garden. Against the Aurelian Walls on piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme are a basilica, a Roman amphitheatre built into the wall line, the remains of an imperial palace and its circus, and three museums. Elsewhere in the rione are churches from the thirteenth century to 1928, a gate of the Servian Walls now called the Arco di Gallieno, two Roman nymphaea and the Scala Santa. Via Merulana is the line with the rione Monti: its east side is Esquilino, its west side is not.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Stazione di Roma Termini stands inside the rione, on piazza dei Cinquecento, which is also a bus terminus: it.wikipedia records 25 daytime lines, including trolleybus line 90, and 13 night lines, with the tram 5 and 14 terminus between via Cavour and via Daniele Manin. The main part of the rebuilt square reopened on 14 January 2025 and the works are programmed to complete in summer 2026, so the layout will keep changing. For the rione's southern churches, the friary of Sant'Antonio da Padova gives its own approaches as metro A at Manzoni, metro B at Colosseo, and tram 3 at Manzoni/Merulana.

Beyond that, steer by addresses. Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II 78 for the Museo Ninfeo and 12/A for the church of Sant'Eusebio. Via Principe Amedeo 184 for the Nuovo Mercato Esquilino, which has four entrances, on via Principe Amedeo, via Mamiani, via Turati and via Lamarmora. Via Merulana 121 for Palazzo Merulana and 124 for the basilica of Sant'Antonio da Padova. Largo Leopardi for the Auditorium di Mecenate, and via di San Vito for the Arco di Gallieno and the church of Santi Vito e Modesto, whose parish address is via Carlo Alberto 47. Piazza Manfredo Fanti 47 for the Acquario Romano.

On piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme the numbers run close together: 9/A for the Museo nazionale degli strumenti musicali, 9 for the Museo storico della fanteria and 7 for the Museo storico dei granatieri di Sardegna. Then via Tasso 145 for the Museo storico della Liberazione, viale Manzoni 47 for Villa Altieri, via Giovanni Giolitti 154 for Santa Bibiana, via Guglielmo Pepe 45 for the Teatro Ambra Jovinelli, and via Principe Eugenio 65/67 for the Palazzo del Freddo Giovanni Fassi.

sections.heading: Opening hours, tickets and booking
sections.body:
Four places in the rione publish hours, and they are the ones to plan around. The Museo nazionale degli strumenti musicali gives Tuesday to Sunday 09:30 to 19:30, last entry 18:30, at 6.00 euro full and 2.00 euro reduced for 18- to 25-year-olds who are EU students, free under 18 and free on the first Sunday of every month, and it is in the Roma Pass and Roma & Più Pass circuit. Palazzo Merulana gives hourly entry slots from 12:00 to 20:00 Wednesday to Friday and 10:00 to 20:00 on Saturday and Sunday, last entry 19:00 on both, with its sculpture hall, CafeCulture and BookCulture open Wednesday to Sunday 09:00 to 20:00 and free to enter. The basilica of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme gives 7:30 to 19:00 and states that entry is free and needs no booking, and that tourist visits are not permitted during liturgical celebrations. The museum inside the basilica, entered from the sacristy, opens every day 10:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 17:30.

Three Roman sites are entered by appointment rather than at a door. The Sovrintendenza Capitolina allows the Auditorium di Mecenate to accompanied groups only, a maximum of thirty people per visit, with booking obligatory on 060608 between 09:00 and 19:00, and individual visits on a published calendar by booking on the same number; the Sepolcri repubblicani di via Statilia work the same way with a maximum of fifteen. The Ninfeo di Alessandro, the ruin called the Trofei di Mario in the piazza Vittorio garden, is given as visitable on request on the same number, and the Ipogeo degli Aureli as visitable on request. The parish of Sant'Eusebio runs a bookable guided-visit programme with two itineraries, including an underground archaeological area.

Two cautions. The Museo storico della fanteria on piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme is recorded by Italian Wikipedia as closed since 2023, with part of its spaces used for art exhibitions, citing la Repubblica of 14 January 2025 and imuseidiroma.it. And the monastic garden inside the oval of the Anfiteatro Castrense is not a public park: the basilica's own site states that it is held on concession by the parish, is used for pastoral activities, and that free access by visitors is not allowed. For the Scala Santa, the Museo Ninfeo, Villa Altieri and the Museo storico dei granatieri di Sardegna, no source states opening hours, so none are given here.

faq.question: Is Santa Maria Maggiore in Esquilino?
faq.answer: No. The basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore stands in the rione Monti, and so does the obelisk behind it. The rione line runs through the square in front of the basilica. The fountain standing on that square is a separate object, which it.wikipedia files in the rione Esquilino.

faq.question: Is Termini station in Esquilino?
faq.answer: Yes. Stazione di Roma Termini stands in the rione Esquilino, on piazza dei Cinquecento. The square itself is a straddle: its own source places it on the border between Esquilino and Castro Pretorio. The monument to the dead of the battle of Dogali that stands on the square is in Castro Pretorio.

faq.question: Is the Scala Santa part of the Vatican?
faq.answer: No. The Scala Santa stands on piazza di San Giovanni in Laterano, in the rione Esquilino, on Italian soil. The Holy See's own published list of its extraterritorial properties in Rome names it in its first item, «il complesso di S. Giovanni in Laterano (Basilica, Palazzo Apostolico Lateranense con gli edifici annessi e la Scala Santa)», and Annex II, Tavola 1 of the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929 names it too. Article 15 of that treaty provides that such property, «benché facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» — although forming part of the territory of the Italian State — enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the seats of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is not Vatican City, it is not a border, and a visitor there is under Italian law.

faq.question: What has to be booked in advance?
faq.answer: The Auditorium di Mecenate at largo Leopardi and the Sepolcri repubblicani di via Statilia are both open to accompanied groups only, thirty people a visit for the first and fifteen for the second, with booking obligatory on 060608 between 09:00 and 19:00; individual visits are possible on a published calendar by booking on the same number. The Ninfeo di Alessandro in the piazza Vittorio garden and the Ipogeo degli Aureli on via Luzzatti are both given as visitable on request, and the parish of Sant'Eusebio runs a bookable guided-visit programme with two itineraries.

faq.question: Which museums in the rione publish prices?
faq.answer: One. The Museo nazionale degli strumenti musicali, at Piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme 9/A, gives 6.00 euro full and 2.00 euro reduced for 18- to 25-year-olds who are EU students, free under 18 and free on the first Sunday of every month, and telephone +39 06 7014796. Palazzo Merulana publishes hours and entry slots but no admission price. For the Museo Ninfeo, Villa Altieri and the two military museums on piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, no admission prices are stated, so none are given here.

faq.question: Can you go inside the Anfiteatro Castrense?
faq.answer: No visiting terms are published for the amphitheatre, and its oval is occupied by the monastic garden of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, which the basilica's own site says is held on concession by the parish, used for pastoral activities, and not open to free access by visitors. What you can see is the outside: the Aurelian Walls cut the amphitheatre in half and turned it into a forward bastion by blocking the arches of its façade, and the wall line runs past it on viale Castrense.

places.name: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II
places.address: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: The porticoed square at the centre of the rione, laid out under the 1873 master plan and built from 1880. it.wikipedia gives it as 325 by 185 metres and 60,000 square metres including the porticoes. The garden in the middle is dedicated to Nicola Calipari and reopened on 31 October 2020 after twenty months of works; three separate things stand inside it, the Severan nymphaeum called the Trofei di Mario, the Porta Alchemica, and Mario Rutelli's fountain of 1911.
places.history: The garden was opened to the public on Sunday 10 July 1889. Open-air market stalls stood on the square from the 1890s until they were cleared in October 2001. The building between via Emanuele Filiberto and via Conte Verde was rebuilt and re-inaugurated in 2012 and houses the Fondazione ENPAM; the excavation carried out for that rebuilding produced the Museo Ninfeo, which opened on 6 November 2021.

places.name: Fontana di piazza Vittorio Emanuele II
places.address: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A fountain of 1911 by the sculptor Mario Rutelli, standing in the garden of piazza Vittorio Emanuele II and known in Rome as «il fritto misto». It was restored in 2020.
places.history: it.wikipedia's article on the square carries the fountain in its own infobox and image captions, giving Mario Rutelli as the sculptor and 1911 as the date.

places.name: Ninfeo di Alessandro (Trofei di Mario)
places.address: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A Severan monumental fountain standing in the garden of piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, which worked both as a display fountain and as a distribution tank, a castellum aquae. Its plan is trapezoidal; it.wikipedia gives it as 25 metres wide, about 20 metres high originally, and 4,000 cubic metres. The Sovrintendenza Capitolina manages it, and the same article gives it as visitable on request, on 060608.
places.history: The two marble trophies that gave the ruin its medieval name, the Trofei di Mario, were moved in 1590 by Sixtus V to the balustrade at the top of the Cordonata on the Campidoglio, where they still are.

places.name: Porta Alchemica (Porta Magica)
places.address: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A stone doorway carved with alchemical inscriptions, standing in the garden of piazza Vittorio Emanuele II and flanked by two statues of the Egyptian god Bes.
places.history: It was built between 1655 and 1681 by Massimiliano Savelli Palombara, marchese di Pietraforte, who lived from 1614 to 1685, in the grounds of his villa Palombara on the Esquiline, and re-erected in the present garden. The villa had five gates and this is the one that survives; an inscription on the lost gate opposite carried the date 1680.

places.name: Museo Ninfeo
places.address: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II 78, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A museum over an excavated sector of the Horti Lamiani, a luxurious private residence which the museum's own site dates between the 1st century BC and the 6th century AD, found during the rebuilding of the ENPAM palazzo on piazza Vittorio Emanuele II. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: It opened to the public on 6 November 2021, under an agreement between the Fondazione ENPAM and the Soprintendenza Speciale Archeologia Belle Arti e Paesaggio di Roma.

places.name: Nuovo Mercato Esquilino
places.summary: A covered market occupying the block of the former Caserma Sani, with four entrances, on via Principe Amedeo, via Mamiani, via Turati and via Lamarmora. mercatidiroma.com gives the address as via Principe Amedeo 184. No opening hours are published for it, so none are given here.
places.history: The block was previously occupied by the Centrale del Latte di Roma and the Caserma Sani, formerly the Caserma Pepe. mercatidiroma.com records a first re-organisation of the market in 1913. The open-air stalls that had stood on piazza Vittorio Emanuele II since the 1890s were cleared in October 2001.

places.name: Chiesa di Sant'Eusebio all'Esquilino
places.address: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II 12/A, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A titular church and parish on piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, wedged among the blocks of the 1873 master plan. The parish's own site gives the address as Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II 12/A, 00185 Roma, and the telephone as 06-44 66 170, and carries a bookable guided-visit programme with two itineraries, including an underground archaeological area.
places.history: it.wikipedia gives the consecration as 1238, by Gregory IX, after a rebuilding a fundamentis, and describes the church as titular and parochial and not a minor basilica. The Celestines, who had held it, abandoned it in the early fourteenth century.

places.name: Stazione di Roma Termini
places.summary: The railway station on piazza dei Cinquecento, standing in the rione Esquilino. Figures attributed to Grandi Stazioni give about 150 million visitors a year and 850 trains a day.
places.history: The station opened in 1863 as the Stazione Centrale delle Ferrovie Romane, was rebuilt in 1873 and rebuilt again in 1950. The present front block is by Eugenio Montuori and Annibale Vitellozzi, 1950; of Angiolo Mazzoni's scheme of the 1930s only the technical buildings were carried out.

places.name: Piazza dei Cinquecento
places.summary: The square in front of Termini station, bounded by via Giovanni Giolitti, largo di Villa Peretti and via Marsala; it.wikipedia gives its surface as 45,000 square metres, citing artribune. The lead of that article places the square «al confine tra i rioni Esquilino e Castro Pretorio», so it is a straddle. The bus terminus around it is used by 25 daytime lines, including trolleybus line 90, and 13 night lines; the tram 5 and 14 terminus lies between via Cavour and via Daniele Manin.
places.history: The square is named for the more than five hundred Italian dead of the battle of Dogali. The main part of the rebuilt square reopened on 14 January 2025, and the works are programmed to complete in summer 2026.

places.name: Monumento a Giovanni Paolo II
places.summary: A bronze statue of John Paul II standing on piazza dei Cinquecento, in front of Termini station.
places.history: it.wikipedia's article on the monument gives the sculptor as Oliviero Rainaldi.

places.name: Acquario Romano — Casa dell'Architettura
places.summary: A nineteenth-century aquarium building on piazza Manfredo Fanti, owned by Roma Capitale and used since 2002 as the seat of the Casa dell'Architettura of the Ordine degli Architetti di Roma. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: It was built between 1885 and 1887 to the design of Ettore Bernich, on land the comune granted in 1882 to the ichthyologist Pietro Garganico for a fish-breeding station and aquarium, and laid out with a pond and small bridges outside on the model of the Paris squares. It was restored between 1985 and 2002.

places.name: Piazza Manfredo Fanti
places.summary: A rectangular square framed by via Principe Amedeo, via Carlo Cattaneo and via Filippo Turati, laid out as a garden around the Acquario Romano and known colloquially as piazza dell'Acquario.
places.history: Remains of the agger of the Servian Walls survive in the square. it.wikipedia calls them «i resti dell'Agger Tarquinii, un tratto delle Mura Serviane» and captions an image of them «Resti dell'agger delle mura serviane».

places.name: Porta Esquilina (Arco di Gallieno)
places.address: Via di San Vito, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A monumental gate of the Servian Walls standing on via di San Vito, now abutted by the church of Santi Vito e Modesto.
places.history: The gate belongs to the earliest circuit of the city's walls and was rebuilt saxo quadrato in 378 BC.

places.name: Chiesa dei Santi Vito e Modesto
places.summary: The church that abuts the Arco di Gallieno, its main door on via di San Vito and its parish address on via Carlo Alberto 47. Over the altar of Saints Crescentia and Modestus is a fresco of the Madonna between them, dated 1483; the parish attributes it to Antoniazzo Romano, and Italian Wikipedia attributes it to Melozzo da Forlì and Antoniazzo Romano.
places.history: The church is first named as a diaconia in the life of Leo III, between the eighth and ninth centuries. Sixtus IV rebuilt it, with 1477 given for the end of the work; it was restored again in the seventeenth century and in the mid-nineteenth by Pietro Camporese il Giovane. Around 1900 Alfredo Ricci reoriented it with a new façade on via Carlo Alberto, and the restoration of the 1970s undid that and returned the main entrance to via di San Vito. Leo XII erected the parish of Santa Maria Maggiore in San Vito here on 1 November 1824, by the bull Super universam. The church stands on the site of the Macellum Liviae, the commercial complex Augustus built on the Esquiline and dedicated to Livia, of which nothing is standing.

places.name: Chiesa di Sant'Antonio Abate all'Esquilino
places.summary: A Russian Greek-Catholic church of the Byzantine rite on via Carlo Alberto, with an iconostasis by the painter Gregorio Maltzeff.
places.history: The church was built in 1308 in place of the earlier Sant'Andrea Catabarbara and rebuilt from 1481 under Sixtus IV; a hospital for St Anthony's fire stood beside it from the second half of the thirteenth century. In 1928 the Holy See bought the church and its adjacencies, the church went to Russian Catholics of the Byzantine rite, and the annexed buildings were turned into the Pontificio Collegio Russicum, a centre of Russian and oriental studies. Sant'Andrea Catabarbara, the church this one replaced, had been made in the second half of the fifth century under Simplicius out of a hall of the Basilica di Giunio Basso, the domus of Junius Annius Bassus, consul of 331, which the Gothic general Valila gave for the purpose; it was demolished in 1930 for the Seminario Pontificio di Studi Orientali in via Napoleone III, and parts of it were incorporated into Sant'Antonio Abate.

places.name: Oratorio di Santa Maria Immacolata della Concezione e monastero delle Viperesche
places.address: Via di S. Vito 10, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: An oratory in via di San Vito, annexed to the house long known as the monastero delle Viperesche. santissimaconcezione.org gives the address as Via di S. Vito 10, 00185 Roma, and the buildings are in use as a women's university college.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates the oratory to 1656 and quotes Armellini, writing in 1891: the oratory is annexed to the monastero delle Viperesche, a house founded by Livia Vipereschi in 1668 by the arch of San Vito to take in poor girls, with an annual income of 300 scudi. The lay teachers later took the habit and the rule of the Carmelite Oblates under the title of the Immaculate Conception. Pius VII restored the oratory, which has three altars, the high altar carrying an image of the Conception. In 1869 the institution became the Convitto Vipereschi della Santissima Concezione, and works in 1930 restored the fronts on via di San Vito and via Sant'Antonio all'Esquilino.

places.name: Chiesa di Sant'Alfonso all'Esquilino
places.summary: A neo-Gothic rectory church on via Merulana, held with its convent by the Redemptorists. The brick and travertine façade carries a portico of three doors, a polychrome mosaic of the Virgin of Perpetual Succour in the tympanum, a Carrara marble statue of the Redeemer on the tympanum's cusp, and a rose window. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: It was built between 1855 and 1859 to the design of the Scottish architect George Wigley. The church is dedicated to the Most Holy Redeemer and is known by the name of Alphonsus Liguori. it.wikipedia places it in via Merulana and gives no street number.

places.name: Auditorium di Mecenate
places.summary: Despite the name this is a nymphaeum: a half-sunken rectangular hall of 24.10 by 10.60 metres, with an apse at one short end, six niches a side and five more in the apse above seven curved steps faced in cipollino marble. The monument stands inside the public garden at Largo Leopardi, off via Merulana. Entry is allowed to accompanied groups only, a maximum of thirty people per visit, and booking is obligatory on 060608 between 09:00 and 19:00; individual visits are also possible on a published calendar, again by booking on the same number.
places.history: The hall was part of the Horti Maecenatis. It was excavated in 1874 by Rodolfo Lanciani, and the Sovrintendenza Capitolina has it in charge.

places.name: Palazzo Merulana
places.summary: The exhibition building of the Fondazione Elena e Claudio Cerasi, at Via Merulana 121: its own site gives 1,800 square metres over four exhibition floors and 90 works of the Scuola Romana and the Italian twentieth century. Hours are hourly entry slots from 12:00 to 20:00 Wednesday to Friday and 10:00 to 20:00 on Saturday and Sunday, last entry 19:00 on both; the sculpture hall, CafeCulture and BookCulture open Wednesday to Sunday 09:00 to 20:00, with free access.
places.history: The building stands on the east frontage of via Merulana, which is the Esquilino side of the street; the west frontage is the rione Monti.

places.name: Basilica di Sant'Antonio da Padova all'Esquilino
places.summary: A minor basilica on via Merulana, also called Sant'Antonio al Laterano. The friary's own site gives the address as via Merulana 124 and its approaches as metro A at Manzoni, metro B at Colosseo and tram 3 at Manzoni/Merulana.
places.history: It was built between 1884 and 1888 by Luca Carimini, for Bernardino da Portogruaro and the Order of Friars Minor, who came here after being expropriated of their convent at the Ara Coeli for the building of the monument to Victor Emmanuel II. Pius XI raised it to minor basilica in July 1931.

places.name: Scala Santa e Sancta Sanctorum
places.address: Piazza di San Giovanni in Laterano, Roma RM
places.summary: The sanctuary on piazza di San Giovanni in Laterano holding twenty-eight white marble steps sheathed in wood, flanked by four further flights, which pilgrims climb on their knees. The complex also holds the chapel of San Lorenzo in Palatio, called the Sancta Sanctorum, which was the popes' private chapel until the early fourteenth century and which holds the Lateran Acheropita; the chapel of San Lorenzo; the oratory of San Silvestro in Palatio; and the chapel of the Crucifix behind the Sancta Sanctorum. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The building is the complex Sixtus V raised at the end of the sixteenth century as the new patriarchate, built by Domenico Fontana in 1589. The sanctuary's own site records that the Passionists were called to its custody by Pius IX in 1854. The Scala Santa is named in the Holy See's own published list of its extraterritorial properties in Rome, whose first item reads «il complesso di S. Giovanni in Laterano (Basilica, Palazzo Apostolico Lateranense con gli edifici annessi e la Scala Santa)», and in Annex II, Tavola 1 of the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Article 15 of that treaty provides that such property, «benché facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» — although forming part of the territory of the Italian State — enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the seats of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It stands on Italian soil, in the rione Esquilino, and visitors there are subject to Italian law.

places.name: Monumento a San Francesco d'Assisi
places.summary: A bronze group at the start of via Carlo Felice, facing the basilica of San Giovanni in Laterano: the saint stands with his arms raised and his palms turned toward the basilica, on a stepped tufa base, with five further figures below.
places.history: The group is by Giuseppe Tonnini and dates from 1927. The five figures below the saint represent the companions who followed him to Rome to seek Innocent III's recognition of the Rule.

places.name: Basilica di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme
places.address: Piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: The basilica's own site places it «a Roma, nel Rione Esquilino, a ridosso delle Mura Aureliane e dell'Anfiteatro Castrense, tra la Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano e Porta Maggiore», and records that Santa Croce is part of the visiting circuit of the Seven Churches. The same site gives its opening hours as 7:30 to 19:00, and states that entry to the basilica is free and needs no booking. During liturgical celebrations tourist visits are not permitted.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that Pius X erected the parish here on 13 March 1910 and that Cistercians have been resident since the sixteenth century. The basilica is not among the Holy See's extraterritorial properties in Rome; it does not appear on that published list.

places.name: Orto monastico di Santa Croce
places.address: Piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: The kitchen-and-flower garden of the Cistercian monastery of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, recreated inside the oval of the Anfiteatro Castrense in 2004 to a design by the architect Paolo Pejrone, on the initiative of the Associazione Amici di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme. It is an elliptical space divided by two perpendicular pergola paths that meet at a central fountain. The basilica's own site states that the garden is held on concession by the parish, is used for pastoral activities, and that free access by visitors is not allowed.
places.history: The garden occupies the arena of a Roman amphitheatre that the Aurelian Walls cut in half in the third century.

places.name: Anfiteatro Castrense
places.address: Piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: An elliptical Roman amphitheatre built into the line of the Aurelian Walls beside Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, 88 by 75.80 metres, with a surface given by it.wikipedia as 5,239 square metres. No visiting terms are published for it, and its oval is occupied by the monastic garden of the basilica, which the basilica's own site says is not open to free access by visitors.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates it to 218-222 AD and says that «con tutta probabilità fu costruito dall'imperatore Eliogabalo … come anfiteatro di corte annesso alla dimora imperiale sessoriana». It stayed in use until the Aurelian Walls cut it in half and turned it into a forward bastion by blocking the arches of its façade. The Sovrintendenza Capitolina records that the elevation was originally three orders of arcades, entirely in brick, and was reduced to the first order for defensive reasons under Paul IV in the sixteenth century, and that the concrete foundations are exposed today because the surrounding ground level dropped.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria del Buon Aiuto
places.address: Piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A small church on piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, built against the Aurelian Walls and the Anfiteatro Castrense, and dependent on the basilica of Santa Croce.
places.history: Sixtus IV raised it in 1476, as the inscription over the door records: Sixtus IV fundavit MCCCCLXXVI.

places.name: Palazzo Sessoriano
places.summary: The imperial residence known as the Sessorium, inside the Horti Variani at the south-east edge of the Augustan Regio V Esquiliae, beside the Aqua Claudia. it.wikipedia gives its surface as 122,500 square metres. It is under the Soprintendenza Speciale Archeologia Belle Arti e Paesaggio di Roma. No source states opening arrangements, so none are given here.
places.history: The complex was begun by Septimius Severus and finished under Elagabalus. The Anfiteatro Castrense and the Circo Variano belonged to the same imperial residential complex, which was called Ad Spem Veterem.

places.name: Terme Eleniane
places.summary: The baths named for Helena, the mother of Constantine, which stood beside Santa Croce in Gerusalemme. Nothing of them is standing: what survived was demolished at the end of the sixteenth century by Domenico Fontana, for Sixtus V, to open the stretch of the strada Felice in front of Santa Croce, which is today's via di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme.
places.history: The baths are of Severan date, on the evidence of the earliest brick stamps and a dedication to Julia Domna found on the site. Helena restored them after a fire in 323-326; her dedication, CIL VI 1136, is now in the Vatican Museums. The plan is known from Renaissance drawings by Palladio and Giuliano da Sangallo.

places.name: Circo Variano
places.summary: The circus of the imperial residential complex called Ad Spem Veterem, which also comprised the Palazzo Sessoriano and the Anfiteatro Castrense. It was originally 630 metres long and 125 metres wide and was later reduced to 565 metres; the western, starting side was found inside the Aurelian Walls and the curved eastern end lay at via Alcamo.
places.history: The circus is named for Elagabalus, Sesto Vario Avito Bassiano. It was begun by Septimius Severus, who reigned from 193 to 211, and completed by Elagabalus, 218-222. The obelisk that stood on its spina, the Antinous obelisk, is now on the Pincio. The northern side later carried the last stretch of the Acqua Felice. It was last excavated in 1959.

places.name: Museo nazionale degli strumenti musicali
places.address: Piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme 9/A, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A state museum of musical instruments in the Palazzina Samoggia, its entrance beside the basilica of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme. Its own site gives Tuesday to Sunday 09:30 to 19:30, last entry 18:30; admission 6.00 euro full and 2.00 euro reduced for 18- to 25-year-olds, EU students only, free under 18, and free on the first Sunday of every month. It is in the Roma Pass and Roma & Più Pass circuit. Telephone +39 06 7014796.
places.history: The museum's own site styles the directorate that runs it the Direzione Musei nazionali della città di Roma; it.wikipedia uses «Direzione Musei statali di Roma» for the transfer of December 2019. it.wikipedia gives 15,770 visitors in 2018, citing the MiBAC visitor-and-receipts table.

places.name: Museo storico dei granatieri di Sardegna
places.address: Piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme 7, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: The regimental museum of the Granatieri di Sardegna, on piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme. No opening hours are published for it, so none are given here.
places.history: The regimental collections were joined on 5 March 1903 in rooms of the Caserma Ferdinando di Savoia. A move to the Caserma Umberto I on piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme was proposed in 1912 and deferred by the First World War, and in 1920 the comune resolved to donate the land.

places.name: Museo storico della fanteria
places.address: Piazza Santa Croce di Gerusalemme 9, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: The infantry museum on piazza Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, under the Comando Brigata meccanizzata «Granatieri di Sardegna». Italian Wikipedia records that the museum has been closed since 2023, with part of its spaces used for art exhibitions, citing la Repubblica of 14 January 2025 and imuseidiroma.it.
places.history: President Giovanni Gronchi inaugurated the museum on 11 November 1959.

places.name: Museo della Basilica di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme
places.address: Piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A museum inside the basilica of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, entered from the sacristy. The basilica's own hours page gives it as visitable every day, 10:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 17:30.
places.history: The basilica's site records that the museum was created in 1999 inside the spaces of the Convent of Santa Croce. The thirteenth- and fourteenth-century frescoes detached from the oratory of Santa Margherita are kept here.

places.name: Oratorio di Santa Margherita
places.summary: A deconsecrated oratory on viale Carlo Felice, set inside the fourth tower of the Aurelian Walls and known also as the prigione di santa Margherita. No visiting arrangements are published for it, so none are given here.
places.history: The tower was converted to an oratory in the Middle Ages and painted with a thirteenth- to fourteenth-century fresco cycle of St Paul and St Margaret of Antioch. The cycle was discovered in 1932, detached, and is now kept in the museum of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme; a recovery project is under way with the aim of returning the frescoes in loco. A Madonna Bona lived in the tower as a recluse in the thirteenth century, and the oratory was still officiated in the seventeenth century, when Clement IX granted indulgences there. Antonio Muñoz restored it in 1914, and it was restored again in 1978.

places.name: Tempio di Minerva Medica
places.summary: A domed monumental hall on via Giovanni Giolitti, wedged between the railway approaches to Termini and the blocks built for the new rione at the end of the nineteenth century, and visible from trains. Despite the name it is not a temple: it stood inside the precinct of a luxurious suburban residence, whose horti are argued as either the Horti Liciniani or the Horti Pallantiani. it.wikipedia dates it to the beginning of the fourth century and gives it as 24 metres high today and 32 metres originally, 25 metres wide, and about 470 square metres.
places.history: The hall is under the Soprintendenza Speciale Archeologia Belle Arti e Paesaggio di Roma, and it.wikipedia records openings on the occasion of special events.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Bibiana
places.summary: A church on via Giovanni Giolitti, standing on the site of the Horti Liciniani. Its façade and its statue of the saint are by Gian Lorenzo Bernini.
places.history: Two traditions of foundation are recorded: 363, by the matron Olimpina, and 467 under Simplicius, per the Liber pontificalis. Leo II translated the relics of the martyrs Simplicius, Faustinus and Beatrice here. Honorius III restored the church in 1224 and added a women's monastery beside it, and Urban VIII ordered its complete rebuilding.

places.name: Sepolcri repubblicani di via Statilia
places.summary: Republican tombs at the corner of via Statilia and via di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme. The Sovrintendenza Capitolina allows entry to accompanied groups only, a maximum of fifteen people per visit, with booking obligatory on 060608 between 09:00 and 19:00; individual visits are also possible on a published calendar, by booking on the same number.
places.history: The tombs were found in 1916. They date to about 100 BC and were buried in the following century, and they were originally aligned along the ancient road also called the via Celimontana, which ran from the Porta Maggiore area toward the Celio. The tomb dated to about the middle of the first century BC takes the form of an ancient altar in blocks of tufa and peperino. Immediately opposite is a small underground area with the remains of two ancient water conduits in hollowed, interlocking tufa blocks.

places.name: Ipogeo degli Aureli
places.summary: A privately held catacomb on the ancient via Labicana, on two levels, with a fresco cycle whose reading remains open. It is under the Pontificia commissione di archeologia sacra, and it.wikipedia gives it as visitable on request.
places.history: It was found in 1919 at the junction of viale Manzoni and via Luzzatti, and it is mentioned in no ancient source.

places.name: Arco di Sisto V (arco Felice)
places.summary: A commemorative arch at piazzale Sisto V, built into the Acqua Felice aqueduct where its final stretch runs over the Aurelian Walls, at the crossing of the two roads that led to Santa Maria Maggiore and to Santa Croce in Gerusalemme. Its own article's lead places it «nel rione Esquilino».
places.history: The arch was made in 1585, in the first year of Sixtus V's pontificate, celebrating the completion of the Acqua Felice. It is known as the arco Felice «dal nome di battesimo del papa committente, Felice Peretti» — from the baptismal name of the pope who commissioned it.

places.name: Porta Tiburtina (Porta San Lorenzo)
places.address: Via di Porta Tiburtina, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A gate in the Aurelian Walls, also called Porta San Lorenzo, standing on via di Porta Tiburtina and in the charge of the Sovrintendenza Capitolina. The boundary between the rione and the quartiere Tiburtino beyond it is the street, not the gate, so the gate stands in Esquilino.
places.history: The gate began as an Augustan arch of 5 BC and was built into the Aurelian Walls in 275 AD.

places.name: Villa Altieri
places.summary: A seventeenth-century suburban villa on viale Manzoni, restored between 2009 and 2010 as the Palazzo della cultura e memoria storica, and now holding a small museum together with the library and the historical archive of the Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: It was commissioned in the 1670s by Paluzzo Paluzzi Altieri degli Albertoni, cardinal-nephew of Clement X, from Giovanni Antonio De Rossi, who converted an old farm building. It was sold in 1857 and bought about 1862 by Cardinal Francesco Saverio de Mérode; after the breach of Porta Pia it was leased to the Italian state, which ran a women's penal institution there until 1897, then to the Dorotee, who ran a girls' boarding school in it to 1933, and then to the Figlie di Nostra Signora al Monte Calvario. The Provincia di Roma bought it in 1975.

places.name: Palazzo della Zecca di Stato
places.summary: The State Mint building on via Principe Umberto. It still holds the Scuola dell'Arte della Medaglia. No source states public opening arrangements, so none are given here.
places.history: it.wikipedia's article on the rione, citing the Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato, gives the building as built between 1908 and 1911 to the design of the engineer Carlo Mongini and inaugurated by Victor Emmanuel III on 27 December 1911. It housed the Museo numismatico della Zecca Italiana until 1962, and coin production there ceased in 1999.

places.name: Piazza Dante
places.summary: A square between via Alfieri and via Giusti, dedicated to Dante. A monument to the poet was designed for it and never built. The gardens at its centre are dedicated to Mary and Hasib Begum, who died in a fire in via Buonarroti on 13 January 2007, and they reopened at the beginning of 2021.
places.history: The square was called piazza Leonardo da Vinci until 1945, because Dante was to be given an avenue in the E42 that was never built. During the Second World War it held an underground public air-raid shelter; in the 1980s the underground rooms were taken over by an Enel substation. Palazzo Dante, on the square, has been the unified seat of the Italian intelligence services since May 2019.

places.name: Villa Wolkonsky
places.address: Via Ludovico di Savoia, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: The official residence of the British Ambassador to Italy, on a property covering nearly five hectares of the Esquiline hill, just inside the Aurelian Walls. No source states an access policy for it, so no visiting arrangements are given here.
places.history: The grounds contain thirty-six arches of the aqueduct of Nero, built by the emperor as a spur off the Aqua Claudia of AD 52 to bring water from Subiaco to the Domus Aurea and to the nymphaeum by the temple of the Divine Claudius. Roman tombs are also present in the grounds.

places.name: Teatro Ambra Jovinelli
places.summary: A theatre on via Guglielmo Pepe with a horseshoe hall and two galleries. The theatre's own site gives the address as «Via Guglielmo Pepe, 45 – Roma» and carries a box office and a 2026-27 season; it.wikipedia's infobox gives the address as via Guglielmo Pepe, 43/47.
places.history: It was built for the impresario Giuseppe Jovinelli. After schemes by Pietro Chiodelli and Giacomo Radiconcini, construction began in 1906, and the following year Ulderico Bencivenga took over as designer. The theatre opened on 3 March 1909.

places.name: Palazzo del Freddo Giovanni Fassi
places.summary: A gelateria at Via Principe Eugenio 65/67. Two of its semifreddi are named on its own site, the sanpietrino and the caterinetta.
places.history: it.wikipedia identifies the building as the former villino liberty Calderai-Torlonia, and also names the sanpietrino.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria Immacolata all'Esquilino
places.summary: A neo-Gothic church on via Emanuele Filiberto, its gabled façade twenty-one metres wide, with two flanking towers, and a little over twenty-two metres high at the tip of the cross.
places.history: It was built for the Frati della Carità, the Padri Bigi, from 1901 to 1914, to the design of Antonio Curri, with the engineer Luigi Cortesi directing. The first mass was said on 8 December 1914, and Cardinal Luigi Traglia consecrated the church on 21 April 1942.

places.name: Cappella di Sant'Elena all'Esquilino
places.summary: A neo-Gothic chapel on via Machiavelli, of a single nave, with polychrome glass and a screen dividing the nuns' part of the hall from the faithful's.
places.history: It was built in 1898-1899 to the design of Ettore Genuini, as the church of the convent of the Franciscan Missionaries of Mary when their convent was enlarged. It is dedicated to St Helen after the foundress's own name, Hélène de Chappotin de Neuville, as the inscription over the portal states. A primary school was annexed to it after the war.

places.name: Cappella di Santa Maria Addolorata all'Esquilino
places.address: Via di San Quintino, 00185 Roma RM
places.summary: A richly decorated chapel in via di San Quintino, belonging to the annexed convent of the Figlie di Nostra Signora al Monte Calvario. Over the entrance portal is the phrase Virgini perdolenti, surmounted by a coat of arms carrying the three crosses of Calvary; inside, a screen separates the nuns' part of the liturgical hall from the faithful's.
places.history: The chapel was built in 1928 and renewed in 2001. On the left as one enters is the tomb of Sister Maria Teresina Zonfrilli, who died in the convent on 20 January 1934 and whose cause was introduced by Pius XII in 1957.

places.name: Museo storico della Liberazione
places.summary: A museum of the Nazi-Fascist occupation of Rome, housed in the former SS prison cells at Via Tasso 145. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: it.wikipedia's infobox gives the address as «Via Tasso, 145 - Rione Esquilino». The rooms the museum occupies were used as cells during the occupation.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Margherita Maria Alacoque
places.summary: A church in via Germano Sommeiller. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: it.wikipedia gives the start of building as 1922, its completion as 1925, and the consecration as 1950.

places.name: Fontana di piazza Santa Maria Maggiore (Esquilino)
places.address: Piazza di Santa Maria Maggiore, Roma RM
places.summary: A fountain standing on piazza di Santa Maria Maggiore, which it.wikipedia files in the rione Esquilino. The basilica behind it stands in the rione Monti.
places.history: No source states a history of the fountain, so none is given here.

entries.name: Stazione di Roma Termini
entries.note: Opened in 1863, rebuilt in 1873 and again in 1950; the present front block is by Eugenio Montuori and Annibale Vitellozzi.

entries.name: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II
entries.note: The porticoed square built from 1880, 325 by 185 metres, its garden opened to the public on Sunday 10 July 1889 and reopened on 31 October 2020.

entries.name: Porta Alchemica
entries.note: A doorway carved with alchemical inscriptions, built between 1655 and 1681 for the marchese Massimiliano Savelli Palombara and flanked by two statues of the god Bes.

entries.name: Museo Ninfeo
entries.note: An excavated sector of the Horti Lamiani under the ENPAM palazzo, opened to the public on 6 November 2021.

entries.name: Auditorium di Mecenate
entries.note: A nymphaeum of the Horti Maecenatis in the garden at largo Leopardi; accompanied groups only, thirty people a visit, booking obligatory on 060608.

entries.name: Porta Esquilina (Arco di Gallieno)
entries.note: A gate of the earliest circuit of the Servian Walls, rebuilt saxo quadrato in 378 BC and now abutted by the church of Santi Vito e Modesto.

entries.name: Scala Santa e Sancta Sanctorum
entries.note: Twenty-eight marble steps sheathed in wood, climbed on the knees, in the complex Domenico Fontana built for Sixtus V in 1589.

entries.name: Basilica di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme
entries.note: One of the Seven Churches of the old pilgrimage circuit; its own site gives 7:30 to 19:00, free entry and no booking.

entries.name: Anfiteatro Castrense
entries.note: An amphitheatre of 218-222 AD, 88 by 75.80 metres, cut in half by the Aurelian Walls and turned into a forward bastion by blocking its façade arches.

entries.name: Museo nazionale degli strumenti musicali
entries.note: Tuesday to Sunday 09:30 to 19:30, last entry 18:30; 6.00 euro full, 2.00 euro reduced, free under 18 and on the first Sunday of every month.

entries.name: Tempio di Minerva Medica
entries.note: A domed hall of the early fourth century, 24 metres high today and 32 originally, standing among the railway approaches on via Giolitti.

entries.name: Museo storico della Liberazione
entries.note: A museum of the Nazi-Fascist occupation of Rome, in the former SS prison cells at Via Tasso 145.

entries.name: Palazzo del Freddo Giovanni Fassi
entries.note: A gelateria in the former villino liberty Calderai-Torlonia on via Principe Eugenio, with two semifreddi named on its own site, the sanpietrino and the caterinetta.

entries.name: Nuovo Mercato Esquilino
entries.note: The covered market in the former Caserma Sani, with entrances on via Principe Amedeo, via Mamiani, via Turati and via Lamarmora.

links.note: The neighbour across via Merulana, which holds Santa Maria Maggiore, the Lateran basilica and palace, Santa Prassede and Palazzo Brancaccio.
The rione on the other side of piazza dei Cinquecento, holding the Terme di Diocleziano, Palazzo Massimo and the Dogali monument.
Another rione in this series, beyond the Lateran: the Colosseum, the Celian hill churches and the Villa Celimontana.
The three-day Rome itinerary in this series. Trains into Rome arrive at Termini, which stands inside this rione.
